claim: The chromatin-tracing data consists of the 3D centroid positions of 651 50 kb chromosomal segments quantified for thousands of individual chromosomes in IMR90 cells.
source: Specifically, the nascent transcription state of ~80 genes as well as the 3D centroid positions of 651 50 kb chromosomal segments was quantified for thousands of individual chromosomes in IMR90 cells (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text describing the chromatin-tracing dataset.

claim: The nascent transcription state of approximately 80 genes was quantified for thousands of individual chromosomes in IMR90 cells.
source: Specifically, the nascent transcription state of ~80 genes as well as the 3D centroid positions of 651 50 kb chromosomal segments was quantified for thousands of individual chromosomes in IMR90 cells (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text describing the chromatin-tracing dataset.

claim: Chromatin centered around the promoter shows less variability while transcribed.
source: We observed that chromatin centered around the promoter shows less variability while transcribed, again as determined by the presence of nascent RNA.
evidence: The claim is directly stated based on analysis of the chromatin-tracing data.

claim: When a gene is active, the promoter is on average closer to the surrounding chromatin.
source: we quantified the difference between them and found a similar red cross (Figure 1I), suggesting that when a gene is active the promoter is on average closer to the surrounding chromatin and the distances between nonpromoter chromosomal segments are unperturbed.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1I showing the difference in median physical distances.

claim: The distances between nonpromoter chromosomal segments are unperturbed with transcription.
source: we quantified the difference between them and found a similar red cross (Figure 1I), suggesting that when a gene is active the promoter is on average closer to the surrounding chromatin and the distances between nonpromoter chromosomal segments are unperturbed.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1I.

claim: Active promoters are closer to the centroids of the surrounding chromatin than inactive promoters.
source: Tellingly, we found a definitive difference between active promoters (1) and inactive promoters (0): the active promoters were closer to the centroids of the surrounding chromatin (Figure 1J).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by Figure 1J showing mean distances to local centroids.

claim: Nearly every gene was closer to the centroid with nascent transcription.
source: We found that even though there are overlaps in the distributions in Figure 1J, nearly every gene was closer to the centroid with nascent transcription, suggesting a general phenomenon.
evidence: The claim is stated based on gene-by-gene analysis shown in Figure 1K.

claim: High-activity genes show greater movement with active transcription when compared to low-activity genes.
source: Interestingly, we found that high-activity genes were both less variable (Appendix 1—figure 2A) and showed greater movement with active transcription when compared to the low-activity genes (Appendix 1—figures 2B and 3).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by figures in Appendix 1.

claim: High-activity genes are less variable than low-activity genes.
source: Interestingly, we found that high-activity genes were both less variable (Appendix 1—figure 2A) and showed greater movement with active transcription when compared to the low-activity genes (Appendix 1—figures 2B and 3).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Appendix 1—figure 2A.

claim: The greater movement for high-activity genes is due to larger distances from the centroid when inactive rather than different distances when active.
source: Upon closer inspection (Appendix 1—figure 3A), the greater movement for the high-activity genes was not so much due to a different distance to the local chromatin centroid when active but was instead due to larger distances from the centroid when inactive
evidence: The claim is stated based on analysis shown in Appendix 1—figure 3A.

claim: The distances between genes are consistently smaller with transcription for short genomic distances (<1.5 Mb).
source: We found that the distances between genes were consistently smaller with transcription for short genomic distances (<1.5 Mb), as evidenced by the significant decrease in the (0,1) and (1,1) interactions compared to the (0,0) interaction.
evidence: The claim is stated based on analysis of promoter-promoter distances shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Transcriptional bursting is correlated with the formation of promoter-promoter contacts.
source: Overall, these results suggest transcriptional bursting (or a consequence of bursting) is correlated with the formation of promoter–promoter contacts.
evidence: The claim is stated as a conclusion from the analysis of promoter-promoter distances.

claim: For genomically proximal genes, when both genes are active the mean distances between the promoters are closer to each other.
source: For genomically proximal genes, we observed that when both genes were active the mean distances between the promoters were indeed closer to each other.
evidence: The claim is stated based on gene pair by gene pair analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The difference in mean distance for (0,0)-(1,1) is approximately twice the difference for (0,0)-(0,1).
source: When we compared the (0,0)–(0,1) to (0,0)–(1,1), the later difference was approximately twice the former difference.
evidence: The claim is stated based on comparison of distance differences shown in Figure 2B.

claim: As genomic distance increases, sufficiently separated genes are positioned to different locations with transcription.
source: Interestingly, we observed that as the genomic distance increased, the difference for both seemed to approach a negative value, suggesting that sufficiently separated genes are positioned to different locations with transcription.
evidence: The claim is stated based on analysis of distance changes as a function of genomic distance in Figure 2B.

claim: The spatial separation between genes depends on individual transcriptional bursts.
source: Overall, these analyses provide strong evidence that the spatial separation between genes depends on individual transcriptional bursts.
evidence: The claim is stated as a conclusion from the analysis of promoter-promoter distances.

claim: Genes which are close to each other (MPD <1100 nm) move closer when bursting.
source: These results suggest that the positioning of genes in physical space influences the outcome of pairwise interactions: genes which are close to each other (MPD <1100 nm) move closer when bursting, and genes that are far from each other separate when bursting.
evidence: The claim is stated based on analysis of distance changes as a function of MPD minus expected MPD shown in Figure 2D and E.

claim: Genes that are far from each other separate when bursting.
source: These results suggest that the positioning of genes in physical space influences the outcome of pairwise interactions: genes which are close to each other (MPD <1100 nm) move closer when bursting, and genes that are far from each other separate when bursting.
evidence: The claim is stated based on analysis of distance changes as a function of MPD minus expected MPD shown in Figure 2D and E.

claim: The MPD is predictive of whether genes move toward or away from each other with transcription.
source: In summary, these results suggest that the MPD is predictive of whether genes move toward or away from each other with transcription.
evidence: The claim is stated as a conclusion from the analysis comparing MPD and genomic distance effects.

claim: Genomic distance is unlikely to drive the repositioning phenomenon.
source: If there were a simple relationship between genomic distance and repositioning, one would expect a monotonic trend and therefore it seems unlikely that genomic distance drives this phenomenon.
evidence: The claim is stated based on analysis shown in Figure 2F and G showing non-monotonic trends.

claim: The distance change between genes is stronger for more active genes.
source: Again, the distance change between genes was stronger for more active genes, suggesting these processes also vary depending upon the transcription activity level (Appendix 1—figure 4).
evidence: The claim is stated based on analysis of high-activity vs low-activity genes shown in Appendix 1—figure 4.

claim: For high-activity genes separated by large MPD (>1300 nm), nearly all of them move away from each other when transcriptionally active.
source: Of note for high-activity genes, nearly all of them move away from each other when they were separated by large MPD (>1300 nm), suggesting the process of moving to a different location for transcription may be more deterministic for highly active genes (Appendix 1—figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is stated based on analysis shown in Appendix 1—figure 4E.

claim: The correlation between genes shows a monotonic decay with increasing genomic distance.
source: With approximately a twofold increase at smaller genomic distances, the correlation showed a monotonic decay with increasing genomic distance – the 0.025 plateau persisted with even higher genomic distances (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is stated based on analysis of correlation coefficients shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The increase in co-expression above the asymptotic baseline persists to approximately 2 Mb.
source: The increase in co-expression above the asymptotic baseline persists to ≈2 Mb.
evidence: The claim is stated based on analysis of correlation as a function of genomic distance.

claim: Co-expression of genes is correlated with the single-chromosome distance between those genes.
source: Notably, we observed that co-expression of genes was correlated with the single-chromosome distance between those genes (columns, Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is stated based on analysis shown in Figure 4B examining single-chromosome distances.

claim: Co-expression shows no correlation with genomic distance when single-chromosome distance is controlled.
source: In contrast, we observed no correlation between co-expression and genomic distance (rows).
evidence: The claim is stated based on analysis shown in Figure 4B examining genomic distance while controlling for single-chromosome distance.

claim: Co-expression is driven by the physical distance between genes on individual chromosomes, uncoupled from genomic distance.
source: In summary, these results indicate that co-expression – as quantified through correlations in nascent RNA – is driven by the physical distance between genes on individual chromosomes, uncoupled from genomic distance, which shows no statistical correlation with co-expression.
evidence: The claim is stated as a conclusion from the analysis of single-chromosome distances vs genomic distances.

claim: Active genes exhibit Brownian motion over timescales of 3000 seconds.
source: We quantified the mean squared displacement (MSD, 'Methods') over a timescale of 3000 s and found that the MSD could be fit with a straight line (Figure 4C), suggesting Brownian motion of active genes over these timescales (Bohrer and Xiao, 2020).
evidence: The claim is stated based on MSD analysis shown in Figure 4C and cited reference.

claim: The bursting frequency does not generally change as a function of distance between genes at a 200 nm binning scale.
source: Surprisingly, we found that on a distance binning scale of 200 nm, the metric did not vary, suggesting that the bursting frequency does not generally change as function of distance between genes at this scale (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is stated based on analysis shown in Figure 4D examining burst frequency vs distance.

claim: Removing resolution error results in a 66% increase in correlation for the first distance bin.
source: Removing resolution error associated with light microscopy resulted in a slight increase in the correlation for the first distance bin, resulting in a 66% increase (Figure 4H).
evidence: The claim is stated based on simulation results shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Removing resolution error and using deterministic on times results in a 250% increase in correlation for the first distance bin.
source: We observed a much greater increase across all distances with the first distance bin rising to 250% of its initial value (Figure 4I).
evidence: The claim is stated based on simulation results shown in Figure 4I.

claim: Removing resolution error, deterministic on times, and diffusion leads to an approximately 5-fold increase in correlation for the first distance bin.
source: For the first distance bin, the removal of all sources of error in fixed cell experiments leads to an ≈5-fold increase.
evidence: The claim is stated based on simulation results shown in Figure 4J.

claim: The corrected transcriptional correlation is approximately 0.3 for genes separated by less than 400 nm.
source: By combining this analysis with live-cell imaging, we arrive at a corrected transcriptional correlation of ϕ≈0.3 for genes separated by < 400 nm.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and supported by simulation results in Figure 4J.

claim: The correlation of approximately 0.3 extends over a spatial distance of approximately 400 nm.
source: The correlation is surprisingly high (≈ 0.3) and extends over a spatial distance of ≈ 400 nm.
evidence: The claim is stated based on simulation results removing noise sources.

claim: Individual genes adopt a constrained conformation upon activation.
source: We find that individual genes adopt a constrained conformation and reposition toward the centroid of the surrounding chromatin upon activation.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract as a main finding.

claim: Genes reposition toward the centroid of the surrounding chromatin upon activation.
source: We find that individual genes adopt a constrained conformation and reposition toward the centroid of the surrounding chromatin upon activation.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract as a main finding.

claim: Physical distance between genes on individual chromosomes is the major factor driving co-bursting.
source: Leveraging the variability in distance inherent in single-cell imaging, we show that physical distance – but not genomic distance – between genes on individual chromosomes is the major factor driving co-bursting.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract as a main finding.

claim: Genomic distance is not the major factor driving co-bursting.
source: Leveraging the variability in distance inherent in single-cell imaging, we show that physical distance – but not genomic distance – between genes on individual chromosomes is the major factor driving co-bursting.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract as a main finding.

claim: The correlation of ϕ≈0.3 represents a physical property of human chromosomes.
source: We propose that this surprisingly large correlation represents a physical property of human chromosomes and establishes a benchmark for future experimental studies.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract as a proposed interpretation.

claim: The correlation of ϕ≈0.3 establishes a benchmark for future experimental studies.
source: We propose that this surprisingly large correlation represents a physical property of human chromosomes and establishes a benchmark for future experimental studies.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract as a proposed application.

claim: Ensemble chromosome conformation capture reveals that promoter-promoter contacts (smaller than 1 Mb) form as transcription levels increase.
source: Ensemble chromosome conformation capture seems to support this model by revealing that promoter–promoter contacts (smaller than 1 Mb) form as transcription levels increase (Hsieh et al., 2021; Zhu and Suh, 2020; Hsieh et al., 2020; Levo et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is stated based on cited references to ensemble chromosome conformation capture studies.

claim: Genes on the same chromosome are more co-expressed in individual cells.
source: Indeed, genes on the same chromosome (Deng et al., 2014; Sun and Zhang, 2019; Tian et al., 2020; Quintero-Cadena and Sternberg, 2016; Xu et al., 2019) and genes that share the same (ensemble) topologically associated domain (Tarbier et al., 2020) are more co-expressed in individual cells (RNA).
evidence: The claim is stated based on cited references to single-cell studies.

claim: Genes that share the same topologically associated domain are more co-expressed in individual cells.
source: Indeed, genes on the same chromosome (Deng et al., 2014; Sun and Zhang, 2019; Tian et al., 2020; Quintero-Cadena and Sternberg, 2016; Xu et al., 2019) and genes that share the same (ensemble) topologically associated domain (Tarbier et al., 2020) are more co-expressed in individual cells (RNA).
evidence: The claim is stated based on cited reference to Tarbier et al., 2020.

claim: Correlations were not seen between nascent transcripts.
source: However, correlations were not seen between nascent transcripts (Levesque and Raj, 2013) and the genomic distance between genes was found to show a more dominant role in RNA co-expression than Hi-C contact frequency (Sun and Zhang, 2019).
evidence: The claim is stated based on cited reference to Levesque and Raj, 2013.

claim: Genomic distance shows a more dominant role in RNA co-expression than Hi-C contact frequency.
source: However, correlations were not seen between nascent transcripts (Levesque and Raj, 2013) and the genomic distance between genes was found to show a more dominant role in RNA co-expression than Hi-C contact frequency (Sun and Zhang, 2019).
evidence: The claim is stated based on cited reference to Sun and Zhang, 2019.

claim: Single-cell RNA-seq showed little to no difference in correlation between genes from the same chromosome with increased contact frequency, given similar genomic distance.
source: Furthermore, single-cell RNA-seq showed little to no difference in correlation between genes from the same chromosome with an increased contact frequency, given a similar genomic distance between the two, bringing the strength of the hypothesis into question (Tarbier et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is stated based on cited reference to Tarbier et al., 2020.

claim: Chromatin tracing of an entire chromosome using super-resolution light microscopy provides a spatial map of the chromatin fiber at approximately 100 nm resolution.
source: First, the development of chromatin tracing of an entire chromosome using super-resolution light microscopy provides a spatial map of the chromatin fiber at ≈100 nm resolution (Su et al., 2020; Hu and Wang, 2021).
evidence: The claim is stated based on cited references to chromatin tracing methodology.

claim: Transcriptional bursting of human genes expressed in their native genomic context can be monitored with high spatial and temporal precision for hours.
source: For example, transcriptional bursting of human genes expressed in their native genomic context can be monitored with high spatial and temporal precision for hours (Rodriguez et al., 2019; Wan et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is stated based on cited references to live-cell imaging studies.

claim: The analysis was done on approximately 7600 individual chromosomes and 80 different genes.
source: The analysis was done on ≈7600 individual chromosomes and 80 different genes.
evidence: The claim is stated in the caption of Figure 1.

claim: The observed repositioning may not be a result of enhancer-promoter interaction.
source: the MPD change did not show a general difference with H3K27ac enrichment when compared to other loci lacking H3K27ac (Appendix 1—figure 1B), suggesting that the observed repositioning may not be a result of enhancer–promoter interaction.
evidence: The claim is stated based on analysis of H3K27ac enrichment shown in Appendix 1—figure 1B.

claim: The movement toward the centroid is likely a steric effect.
source: Another possibility – which we favor – is that the movement toward the centroid is a steric effect.
evidence: The claim is stated as a favored interpretation by the authors.

claim: Active genes recruit large megadalton complexes such as the pre-initiation complex and RNA polymerase II.
source: Active genes recruit large megadalton complexes such as the pre-initiation complex and RNA polymerase II, which 'pushes' and confines the gene to a specific location due to the occluded volume effect.
evidence: The claim is stated as part of a mechanistic explanation and is based on established knowledge.

claim: The recruitment of large complexes pushes and confines the gene to a specific location due to the occluded volume effect.
source: Active genes recruit large megadalton complexes such as the pre-initiation complex and RNA polymerase II, which 'pushes' and confines the gene to a specific location due to the occluded volume effect.
evidence: The claim is stated as a proposed mechanism based on physical principles.

claim: Almost all of the approximately 80 genes showed repositioning and confinement behavior.
source: Nevertheless, almost all of the ≈80 genes showed this behavior of repositioning and confinement, suggesting a general phenomenon, illustrating a fundamental aspect of transcription whose mechanistic details await additional study.
evidence: The claim is stated based on analysis of the chromatin-tracing data.

claim: The repositioning and confinement behavior is a general phenomenon.
source: Nevertheless, almost all of the ≈80 genes showed this behavior of repositioning and confinement, suggesting a general phenomenon, illustrating a fundamental aspect of transcription whose mechanistic details await additional study.
evidence: The claim is stated as an inference from the widespread observation across genes.

claim: The rules of promoter-promoter interaction may apply to enhancer-promoter interaction.
source: Considering the functional similarity between promoters and enhancers (Kim and Shiekhattar, 2015), we speculate that the rules of promoter–promoter interaction observed here may apply to enhancer–promoter interaction.
evidence: The claim is stated as speculation based on functional similarity and cited reference.

claim: For MPD < 400 nm, a repositioning of 100 nm could be functionally relevant.
source: In most cases, the distance change of promoters with transcription is small when compared to the MPD, but for MPD < 400 nm a repositioning of 100 nm could be functionally relevant (Figure 2C; Levo et al., 2022; Bohrer et al., 2021; Heist et al., 2019; Chen et al., 2018; Fukaya et al., 2016)
evidence: The claim is stated based on analysis and cited references to relevant studies.

claim: Transcription factories are highly dynamic.
source: On the other hand, transcription factories have also been shown to be highly dynamic (Cisse et al., 2013; Cho et al., 2018; Henninger et al., 2021), raising the question of whether these dynamic promoter–promoter distances are linked to the dynamics of the factories (Heist et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is stated based on cited references to studies of transcription factory dynamics.

claim: The average genomic distance between genes in the Levesque and Raj study was 3 Mb.
source: The fact that the average genomic distance between genes in the previous work was 3 Mb explains why enriched correlations were not seen at the nascent RNA level (Levesque and Raj, 2013).
evidence: The claim is stated to explain previous negative results based on the cited study.

claim: The variability in MPD for a given genomic distance is too low to disentangle these variables.
source: With our finding that the variability in MPD (or contact frequency) for a given a genomic distance is too low to disentangle these variables (Figure 3D and E), the defined enrichments in contact frequency for previous studies were likely quite minor in terms of producing a change in correlation (Tarbier et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is stated based on analysis shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: An enrichment in correlation is observed for genomic distances up to 10 Mb when the physical distance between genes is less than 200 nm on individual chromosomes.
source: This result is illustrated with the extremes: we observed an enrichment in correlation for genomic distances up to 10 Mb when the physical distance between genes was less than 200 nm on individual chromosomes, and very low correlations between genes separated by less than.5 Mb given that the physical distance was above 1200 nm (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is stated based on analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Very low correlations are observed between genes separated by less than 0.5 Mb when the physical distance is above 1200 nm.
source: This result is illustrated with the extremes: we observed an enrichment in correlation for genomic distances up to 10 Mb when the physical distance between genes was less than 200 nm on individual chromosomes, and very low correlations between genes separated by less than.5 Mb given that the physical distance was above 1200 nm (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is stated based on analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The key finding is a correlation gradient with physical distance but not genomic distance.
source: In summary, our key finding is a correlation gradient with physical distance but not genomic distance.
evidence: The claim is stated as a summary of the main finding regarding co-expression.

claim: The lack of temporal data and spatial resolution limits greatly obscure the true transcriptional correlation between spatially proximal genes.
source: The lack of temporal data and the spatial resolution limits of the chromatin-tracing methodology greatly obscures both the 'true' transcriptional correlation between spatially proximal genes and also the length scale over which transcriptional correlation is measured.
evidence: The claim is stated as a limitation of the fixed-cell methodology.

claim: The lack of temporal data and spatial resolution limits obscure the length scale over which transcriptional correlation is measured.
source: The lack of temporal data and the spatial resolution limits of the chromatin-tracing methodology greatly obscures both the 'true' transcriptional correlation between spatially proximal genes and also the length scale over which transcriptional correlation is measured.
evidence: The claim is stated as a limitation of the fixed-cell methodology.

claim: A correlation of approximately 0.3 has been reported between the mRNA levels of adjacent genes in yeast.
source: Intriguingly, this level of correlation has been reported between the mRNA levels of adjacent genes in yeast but was attributed to DNA supercoiling (Patel et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is stated based on cited reference to a yeast study.

claim: The correlation between mRNA levels of adjacent genes in yeast was attributed to DNA supercoiling.
source: Intriguingly, this level of correlation has been reported between the mRNA levels of adjacent genes in yeast but was attributed to DNA supercoiling (Patel et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is stated based on cited reference to Patel et al., 2022.

claim: Other live-cell studies have seen correlated bursts between spatially proximal genes.
source: Furthermore, other live-cell studies have seen correlated bursts between spatially proximal genes (in trans and cis), but did not specifically investigate this as a function of the physical distance between the genes or account for the variable on times (Fukaya et al., 2016; Lim et al., 2018; Heist et al., 2019; Levo et al., 2022)
evidence: The claim is stated based on cited references to live-cell studies.

claim: Previous live-cell studies found enrichments in correlation similar to the uncorrected curve.
source: Furthermore, other live-cell studies have seen correlated bursts between spatially proximal genes (in trans and cis), but did not specifically investigate this as a function of the physical distance between the genes or account for the variable on times (Fukaya et al., 2016; Lim et al., 2018; Heist et al., 2019; Levo et al., 2022) – finding enrichments in correlation similar to the uncorrected curve (Figure 4A; Levo et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is stated based on comparison with cited references.

claim: The enrichment in co-bursting for genes separated by <400 nm suggests the working distance of the underlying mechanism is not direct contact.
source: The enrichment in co-bursting for genes separated by <400 nm suggests the working distance of the underlying mechanism is not direct contact.
evidence: The claim is stated as an inference from the observed distance scale of correlation.

claim: The results are consistent with the idea of enhancers coordinating transcription with working distances of hundreds of nm.
source: Exactly what mechanism leads to these general correlations is still unknown; however, these results are consistent with the idea of enhancers coordinating transcription with working distances of hundreds of nm (Fukaya et al., 2016; Lim et al., 2018; Heist et al., 2019; Levo et al., 2022; Bohrer et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is stated as consistency with cited references on enhancer function.

claim: Co-expression is a general property of the system.
source: The analysis suggests co-expression is a general property of the system, that is, unrelated genes show correlated bursts with each other when in spatial proximity.
evidence: The claim is stated as an interpretation of the analysis results.

claim: Unrelated genes show correlated bursts with each other when in spatial proximity.
source: The analysis suggests co-expression is a general property of the system, that is, unrelated genes show correlated bursts with each other when in spatial proximity.
evidence: The claim is stated as an interpretation of the analysis results.

claim: Transcriptional correlation is an unavoidable emergent behavior due to the physicality of the system.
source: This transcriptional correlation would then be an unavoidable emergent behavior due to the physicality of the system.
evidence: The claim is stated as a proposed interpretation of the correlation phenomenon.

claim: The appearance of correlated bursts may not suggest a specific regulatory mechanism.
source: Hence, the appearance of correlated bursts may not suggest a specific regulatory mechanism.
evidence: The claim is stated as an implication of the emergent behavior hypothesis.

claim: The physical distance between the vast majority of genes arises from the physical constraints of the nucleus and DNA and is not indicative of a biologically functional relationship.
source: Stated another way: we hypothesize that the physical distance between the vast majority of genes arises from the physical constraints of the nucleus and DNA and is not indicative of a biologically functional relationship requiring coordinated expression conferred by that proximity.
evidence: The claim is stated as a hypothesis by the authors.

claim: Disrupting genomic clusters of metabolic genes such as the GAL genes in yeast have no measurable impact on fitness.
source: Support for this hypothesis comes from the observation that disrupting genomic clusters of metabolic genes such as the GAL genes in yeast have no measurable impact on fitness (Lang and Botstein, 2011).
evidence: The claim is stated based on cited reference to support the hypothesis.

claim: There are instances where coordinated co-expression conferred by spatial proximity is important, such as in the segmentation clock genes her1 and her7.
source: Of course, there are certainly instances where coordinated co-expression conferred by spatial proximity is important, for example, in the segmentation clock genes her1 and her7 located on the same chromosome and separated by 12 kb (Zinani et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is stated as an exception to the general hypothesis, based on cited reference.

claim: A theoretical benchmark is established that can be used in future studies.
source: Thus, we establish a theoretical benchmark that can be used in future studies.
evidence: The claim is stated as a contribution of the work.

claim: The majority of genes had average on times between 10 and 15 minutes.
source: This assumption is motivated by our recent work on high-throughput imaging of hundreds of human genes labeled at their endogenous loci using MS2 stem loops – where it was found the majority of genes had an average on times between 10 and 15 min (Wan et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is stated based on cited reference to previous work.

claim: The on time of a human gene is approximately 10-15 minutes.
source: Considering the on time of a human gene – as measured by the dwell time of nascent RNA – is approximately 10–15 min (Wan et al., 2021), we sought to monitor the diffusion of an active gene over a longer timescale.
evidence: The claim is stated based on cited reference to Wan et al., 2021.

claim: Chromatin has been suggested to show confined diffusion.
source: Chromatin has been suggested to show confined diffusion (Marshall et al., 1997; Chubb et al., 2002; Chen et al., 2013; Bronshtein et al., 2015), but this phenomenon is generally quantified over relatively short timescales of <10 min.
evidence: The claim is stated based on cited references to chromatin dynamics studies.

claim: Confined diffusion of chromatin is generally quantified over timescales of less than 10 minutes.
source: Chromatin has been suggested to show confined diffusion (Marshall et al., 1997; Chubb et al., 2002; Chen et al., 2013; Bronshtein et al., 2015), but this phenomenon is generally quantified over relatively short timescales of <10 min.
evidence: The claim is stated based on cited references.
